assessment_summary.cou_name: Substantiate pump setpoint and manifold geometry by demonstrating ≥10 C thermal headroom at worst-case load before CDR

evidence_keywords: Mesh: polyhedral fluid with prism layers (first cell y+ ≈ 0.8 near walls)
Coarse/medium/fine: 8.1M / 12.4M / 20.7M cells.
hotspot on the copper slug moved by −1.9 C (coarse→medium) and −0.6 C (medium→fine)
Residuals to 1e-5 for energy and 1e-4 for momentum
area-averaged inlet/outlet enthalpy rise matched input electrical heat within 0.4% after stabilization.
Solid-side conduction balance closed to within 0.7%.
steady RANS with SST turbulence and full solid-fluid coupling.
No boiling regime modeled; all surfaces remain >10 C below saturation
we are not capturing manifold secondary flows perfectly; a quick unsteady RANS run suggested <1 C impact on peaks
TIM resistance was set to 0.22 K·cm²/W per vendor D5470 data; we bracketed it 0.10–0.40 in a sweep.
Wall roughness for the channels was initially taken as hydraulically smooth; we later ran a case with 5 µm equivalent sandgrain roughness
Coolant properties are temperature-dependent via CoolProp
copper at 385 W/m-K (coupon measurement), 6061-T6 per ASM.
We built a single-cold-plate rig with cartridge heaters under a copper spreader
8 K-type thermocouples epoxied to the plate underside
one RTD on inlet/outlet
FLIR A615 for surface maps; dP via 0–50 kPa differential transducer.
Tin=28.5 C
enthalpy rise matched input electrical heat within 0.4%
model predicted the max device-lid temperature 2.6 C higher than measured
mean of the 8 TC points was +1.3 C vs test.
Predicted pressure drop was 10–12% lower than measured; introducing 5 µm roughness closed half the gap.
